title: Do Not Delay What Is Due

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When you sacrifice a fellowship offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in such a way that it will be accepted on your behalf. It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day; anything left over until the third day must be burned up. If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is impure and will not be accepted. Whoever eats it will be held responsible; they have desecrated what is holy to the LORD, and must be cut off from their people.'" - Lev 19:5-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The fellowship offering was the joyful one — the sacrifice where the worshipper shared a meal in God's presence with family and friends. But it had a time limit. Eat it within two days. After that, it was no longer acceptable.

Why? Partly practical, in a hot climate. But there is something more. God did not want the offering hoarded. This was food meant to be shared quickly and generously — which is exactly why these meals became occasions to invite others in. You could not save it for yourself. You had to spread it around, fast.

There is a principle here about the things God gives us. They are usually meant to move, not to be stored.

Money kept indefinitely becomes an idol. Encouragement stored up and never spoken helps nobody. A gift God gave you to serve others, kept unused for years, quietly spoils.

Jesus told a parable about a man who built bigger barns to store his surplus and died that night (Luke 12:16-21). And the Israelites gathering manna found that what they hoarded bred worms (Ex 16:20).

Whatever God has given you — use it. Share it. Today, not the third day.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God given you that you have been storing rather than using?
2. Is there encouragement you have never actually spoken to someone?
3. Who could you share something with this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for what You have given me. Keep me from hoarding what was meant to be shared, and help me use it generously today. Amen.
